sections.html:
Two city offices touch your bill. The Clerk/Treasurer mails it and collects the money. The City Assessor's Office sets the value it rests on. The Clerk/Treasurer department prepares the bills for property and business owners, takes in real estate taxes and keeps the Board of Review hearing record.

The Assessor's Office discovers, lists and values each taxable property in the city, and it levies nothing. Take a dollar-amount question to the taxing bodies. Take a question about the value on your property record to the assessor.

After July 31 the city passes its real estate tax records to the Waukesha County Treasurer, who collects every delinquent real estate tax. That office is at 515 W. Moreland Blvd., Room AC148, Waukesha, WI 53188, open weekdays 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The phone is 262-548-7029.

The net rate on the 2025 Waukesha tax bills is $13.42 per $1,000 of valuation: a gross rate of $14.46 less a state credit of $1.04. Four taxing bodies share the bill, and the city itself keeps a little over half.

Early each December the rates are set from the taxing bodies' levies, so the coming year's rate shows up on the bill that arrives this winter. Valuation times rate gives a rough bill.

The city offers three installments. Pay everything or the first third by January 31, the second by March 31 and the third by May 31. No further bills follow the first mailing, so keep the installment coupons that come with it.

Current real estate taxes are collected at the Clerk/Treasurer from mid-December through July 31. Due dates are printed on your bill, and 262-524-3850 reaches the office if you want to confirm them.

The three-date plan is unusual. The county's due date table shows January 31 and July 31 for most Waukesha County municipalities, including the separate Waukesha Village entry. Only the City of Waukesha, New Berlin and Sussex follow January 31, March 31 and May 31. Owners near the city line should check which municipality bills the parcel.

Five ways to pay are listed by the city, and a lender can also pay from escrow:

  • Online at tax.waukeshacounty.gov by eCheck ($1.50 fee), debit card ($3.95 fee) or credit card (2.39 percent of the payment).
  • At any Waukesha State Bank branch, with the bill or payment stub. You do not have to be a customer.
  • By mail to Waukesha City Hall, Attn: Clerk/Treasurer Office, 201 Delafield Street, Waukesha, WI 53188, payable to City of Waukesha.
  • In a 24-hour drop box at City Hall or at the Waukesha Public Library, 321 Wisconsin Avenue. Payments left there are processed the next business day.
  • At the Clerk/Treasurer Office on the first floor of City Hall, Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

When your mortgage company pays the tax, ask when it will go out. An escrow check made out to both the city and the homeowner must be signed on the back by every person named, and an escrow overage refund can take four to six weeks by mail.

sections.h2: How does a Waukesha assessment appeal work?
sections.html:
The Waukesha Board of Review takes objections, and the city announces the filing deadline each spring. The yearly sequence: the assessor issues real estate notices, an open book period follows, objections are due at 9:00 a.m. shortly before the first hearing, and that hearing starts at 9:00 a.m. in the Council Chambers at City Hall.

The next assessment date is January 1, 2027, and the assessor's page offers an online Request for Property Review application for it. Under Wis. Stat. 70.32, the assessor values real property at the full value it could ordinarily bring at a private sale.

The assessor's website also provides a property record card for each parcel, showing assessed value, lot size, building details and tax history. Pull yours before listing, because a buyer's agent will look at the same record.

sections.h2: If a Waukesha tax bill goes unpaid
sections.html:
Unpaid tax turns delinquent and begins to carry interest and penalty. Installments only work when each one is paid on time, because a single miss makes the entire remaining balance delinquent (Wis. Stat. 74.11 and 74.12). The charge runs 1.5 percent a month, counted back to February 1, until paid.

A mailed payment is timely under Wis. Stat. 74.69(1) if it is properly addressed, postmarked before midnight on the last day to pay and received by the treasurer within five business days afterward. The only exception is postal delay or administrative error found by a county board committee.

Foreclosure auctions for tax-delinquent property are run by the county treasurer on WisconsinSurplus.com. Behind on tax? Call 262-548-7029 for the payoff before a sale step goes any further.

Obtain the current tax balance from the Clerk/Treasurer or the county treasurer and give it to your closing agent so it shows on the settlement statement. At tax.waukeshacounty.gov you can enter an address or parcel number to see whether a bill is paid.

Two other Wisconsin rules apply around then. A seller of a one to four unit home must give the buyer a completed real estate condition report within 10 days after the contract is accepted, and the statutory form has a section for taxes, special assessments and permits (Wis. Stat. 709.02 and 709.03). If the report is late, the buyer may rescind within two business days after those 10 days run out. A court-appointed fiduciary who never lived in the house is excused from the report.

For a mortgage payoff, a lender must answer a written request within seven business days when the loan is on residential property, and may not describe the payoff amount as subject to change before the payoff date (Wis. Stat. 708.15). Ask early and match the good-through date to your closing date.

Waukesha sits on the Fox River about 15 miles west of Milwaukee. The city calls itself the seventh largest in Wisconsin, with close to 72,000 residents, and the manufacturing hub of Waukesha County. It covers 25.07 square miles, about 24.8 of it land.

Four taxing bodies share each bill here, so ask the Clerk/Treasurer for the figures on your exact parcel instead of relying on a general rate.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Waukesha property tax?
faqs.a: The City of Waukesha Clerk/Treasurer takes payment until July 31: online at tax.waukeshacounty.gov, at a Waukesha State Bank branch, by mail, in a City Hall or library drop box, or at the counter at 201 Delafield Street. After July 31 the Waukesha County Treasurer at 515 W. Moreland Blvd. collects what is still owed.

faqs.q: What is the Waukesha property tax rate?
faqs.a: The net rate on the 2025 bills is $13.42 per $1,000 of valuation. That is the $14.46 gross rate for the city, school district, county and technical college, less a $1.04 state credit. The city's own share is $7.79 per $1,000.

faqs.q: Can I pay Waukesha property tax in installments?
faqs.a: Yes. The city offers three installments, due January 31, March 31 and May 31. Missing one makes the remaining balance delinquent, so pay each on time or pay in full.

faqs.q: Who hears a Waukesha property assessment appeal?
faqs.a: The Board of Review hears it, and the Clerk/Treasurer keeps its record. Watch for the assessment notice the city issues each spring and file before the stated deadline.

faqs.q: What happens to Waukesha taxes after July 31?
faqs.a: The city sends its unpaid real estate tax records to the Waukesha County Treasurer, who collects the delinquent taxes. Interest and penalty of 1.5 percent per month, counted from February 1, apply to delinquent balances.
